entities.summary: Jean-Baptiste Thomas Médée Cécille was a French Admiral and politician who played a pivotal role in the French intervention of Vietnam and completed the first circumnavigation of the globe. As a naval officer, he served under Napoleon Bonaparte and participated in several military campaigns, including the Battle of Trafalgar. Cécille's diplomatic efforts in Vietnam led to the establishment of French trade relations with the country. His naval exploits earned him a reputation as a skilled commander, and he was celebrated as a national hero upon his return to France. "The seas are our inheritance, and our duty is to protect them," Cécille said in a speech to the French Navy, reflecting his enduring legacy as a champion of maritime power. As a key figure in the French Navy during the 19th century, Cécille's impact on French maritime history cannot be overstated.
